content.value_statement: Medical device teams need consistent controls across complex documentation and regulatory requirements. This skill structures document lifecycles, change workflows, reviews, and DMS planning.
actual_capabilities: Structures document control systems across classification, creation, approval, distribution, maintenance, retention, and disposal.
Outlines documentation considerations for EU MDR, FDA submissions, ISO standards, and international markets.
Defines change request, review, implementation, verification, closure, and post-change monitoring stages.
Guides DMS requirements, vendor selection, configuration, validation, deployment, training, and performance monitoring.
Proposes documentation quality metrics, audit activities, and continuous improvement practices.
Covers electronic records, signatures, multilingual documentation, cross-functional coordination, and training.
limitations: Provides general guidance, not legal advice, regulatory approval, or an independent compliance determination.
Includes only a placeholder helper script and does not automate document control workflows.
Lists several guides, scripts, templates, and forms that are not included in the package.
Cannot access a DMS, inspect source records, approve documents, or verify implementation evidence.

use_cases.title: Design a document control framework
use_cases.description: Create a lifecycle model covering document classes, ownership, approvals, distribution, revisions, retention, and disposal.

use_cases.title: Review regulatory documentation coverage
use_cases.description: Map documentation activities to EU MDR, FDA submission, ISO 13485, and related quality requirements.

use_cases.title: Plan a controlled DMS rollout
use_cases.description: Define requirements, selection criteria, validation activities, training, deployment stages, and performance measures.

prompt_templates.title: Assess basic document controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this document control process. Identify missing lifecycle stages, unclear ownership, approval gaps, and practical improvements. Present findings by priority.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a structured review of an existing process.

prompt_templates.title: Build a change control workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a document change workflow for [organization]. Include request data, impact assessment, reviewers, approvals, implementation, training, verification, closure, and monitoring.
prompt_templates.scenario: A quality team needs a repeatable document revision process.

prompt_templates.title: Map regulatory documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a documentation coverage matrix for [device and markets]. Address EU MDR, FDA pathway, ISO 13485, ISO 14971, ownership, evidence, and review status.
prompt_templates.scenario: A regulatory team is preparing documentation across several markets.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a validated DMS program
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop a risk-based DMS implementation plan for [organization]. Include requirements, vendor evaluation, configuration, validation, migration, access controls, audit trails, training, and metrics.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced team needs an implementation plan supporting 21 CFR Part 11 expectations.

output_examples.input: Assess our process: authors email procedures to one manager, who approves them and stores final copies on a shared drive.
output: High priority: define controlled review, approval, versioning, access, and obsolete-copy handling.
Medium priority: assign document owners, review intervals, retention rules, and training records.
Next step: create a document register and a controlled change request workflow.

output_examples.input: Create change control stages for revising a manufacturing work instruction.
output_examples.output: Initiate the request, assess product and regulatory impact, obtain reviews, update the instruction, train affected staff, verify deployment, and close the record.

output_examples.input: Suggest documentation quality indicators for a quarterly management review.
output: Document accuracy: error and correction rates.
Process efficiency: approval cycle time and overdue reviews.
Compliance: audit findings and requirement adherence.
Adoption: training completion and user feedback.

best_practices: Provide the device type, markets, document classes, current workflow, and applicable procedures.
Validate recommendations against current regulations, internal quality procedures, and qualified regulatory advice.
Request named owners, objective evidence, review frequency, and measurable completion criteria.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated guidance as regulatory approval or a complete compliance assessment.
Do not approve changes without impact assessment, authorized review, training, and implementation evidence.
Do not reference unavailable templates or guides without confirming that required resources exist.

faq.question: Which organizations benefit from this skill?
faq.answer: Medical device quality, regulatory, engineering, manufacturing, and document control teams can use its planning frameworks.

faq.question: Does it certify ISO 13485 compliance?
faq.answer: No. It organizes documentation considerations but cannot certify compliance or replace an accredited audit.

faq.question: Can it approve regulatory submissions?
faq.answer: No. Authorized organizational reviewers and regulatory professionals must make submission and approval decisions.

faq.question: Does it automate DMS workflows?
faq.answer: No. The package contains a placeholder script, so its practical value is guidance and planning.

faq.question: Can it support 21 CFR Part 11 planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers validation, authentication, authorization, audit trails, record integrity, retention, and inspection readiness at a planning level.

faq.question: What information improves the output?
faq.answer: Provide device type, target markets, applicable standards, current procedures, DMS constraints, stakeholders, risks, and desired deliverables.
